53.name: Brahmaputra River
53.why: Lohit/Tellu ends on the Brahmaputra start but its Confluence field says Siang, and the Dibang joins the Lohit, so the classic Siang-Lohit-Dibang confluence is declared by hand. GeoNames wrongly places Mankachar in Meghalaya.

803.name: Tsari Chu/ Gelen Bung
803.why: Tibetan river that joins the Subansiri after crossing at Longju. The CWC line starts about 17 km inside the border, beyond the automatic check.

860.name: Jaldhaka
860.why: Rises in East Sikkim, crosses about 40 km of Bhutan and re-enters India at Bindu. The tracer took the Bhutan stretch for the source.

864.name: Dihang/Siang River
864.origin: Tibet, China, as the Yarlung Tsangpo

872.name: Torsa
872.why: Traced source is in remote Tibet with no listed town nearby; the Torsa (Amo Chu) rises in the Chumbi Valley.

950.name: Manas
950.origin: Tibet, China, as the Kuri Chhu
950.why: Its main headstreams rise in Tibet. The traced path starts on a Bhutan border ridge, so the tracer reported a Bhutanese source.

951.name: Burisuti
951.origin: Tibet, China, as the Kuri Chhu
951.why: A channel of the Manas, sharing its catchment.

1844.name: Narmada River
1844.origin: Maikal Range at Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh
1844.end: Gulf of Khambhat, 40 km west of Bharuch, Gujarat
1844.why: Source text: Amarkantak. Mouth is out in the estuary, beyond Bharuch.

2961.name: Bhima River
2961.why: Source text: Bhimashankar. Auto said '70 km E of Mumbai'.

3218.name: Krishna River
3218.end: Krishna delta, south of Repalle, Andhra Pradesh
3218.why: Auto end '90 km S of Vijayawada' was technically right but unhelpful. Origin left automatic: matches source text.

4946.name: Godavari River
4946.origin: Brahmagiri hills (Western Ghats) near Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra
4946.why: Source text: Trambakeshwar. End point is at the Vasishta Godavari mouth by Antarvedi.

5060.name: Indravati River
5060.origin: Eastern Ghats near Thuamul Rampur, Kalahandi district, Odisha

5657.name: Manjra River
5657.origin: Balaghat Range near Patoda, Beed district, Maharashtra

6541.name: Wainganga River
6541.end: Chaparala, Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra, where the Wainganga and Wardha form the Pranhita

6554.name: Wardha River
6554.end: Near Gondpipri, Maharashtra, where the Wardha and Wainganga form the Pranhita

6983.name: Cauvery River
6983.why: Source text: Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri range.

8654.name: Dahisar
8654.origin: Tulsi Lake, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Mumbai
8654.why: Auto labelled it 'Western Ghats near Thane'; it rises in the national park.

8809.name: Mahim
8809.origin: Near Vihar Lake, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Mumbai
8809.why: Line runs from beside Vihar Lake to Mahim Creek: the Mithi's course. The dataset names it after the creek at its mouth.

8969.name: Ulhas
8969.why: User's worked example. GeoNames has no 'Vasai' entry, only Virar and Bhayandar.

8975.name: Savitri
8975.why: Mouth is at Bankot creek by Harihareshwar.

9009.name: Malad Creek
9009.end: Malad Creek, opening to the sea at Versova, Mumbai
9009.why: Drawn on the map, this line rises in the national park and runs through Kandivali East and West before entering Malad Creek: the Poisar's course. The dataset names it after the creek it drains into.

9293.name: Kallada River
9293.why: Auto described a Kerala source relative to Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu.

9727.name: Periyar River
9727.origin: Sivagiri hills, Periyar Tiger Reserve (Western Ghats), Kerala
9727.why: Source text: Sivagiri peak. Auto described it from a Tamil Nadu town.

11076.name: Mahanadi River
11076.origin: Sihawa hills near Nagri, Dhamtari district, Chhattisgarh

11466.name: Subarnarekha River
11466.origin: Chota Nagpur Plateau at Nagri, near Ranchi, Jharkhand
11466.end: Near Talsari, on the Odisha-West Bengal coast

11787.name: Beas River
11787.origin: Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass, Himachal Pradesh

15535.name: Indus River
15535.why: Line starts at the border near Demchok. End follows the source dataset, which runs the line to the edge of Gilgit-Baltistan.

15569.name: Tangtsa
15569.why: The line starts in Pangong Tso, so HydroRIVERS sends the lake basin through it; the lake has no outflow, and the river rises in Ladakh.

15848.name: Satluj River
15848.origin: Rakshastal, near Lake Mansarovar, Tibet, China
15848.why: Source text: Rakshastal, Tibet. Line starts at Shipki La.

15985.name: Mahi River
15985.origin: Vindhya Range near Sardarpur, Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh

16577.name: Luni River
16577.why: Formed where the Sagarmati and Saraswati meet at Govindgarh (the data joins both exactly there).

19186.name: Barak River
19186.origin: Naga Hills near Mao, Senapati district, Manipur
19186.end: Near Karimganj, Assam, where it splits into the Surma and Kushiyara
19186.why: The dataset's end point is identical to its start point, so no automatic end description is possible.

20880.name: Pennar River
20880.why: Source text: Chenna Kasava hill of the Nandidurg range.

21587.name: Banas River
21587.end: Rameshwar, on the Rajasthan-Madhya Pradesh border

22590.name: Chambal River
22590.origin: Janapav hills (Vindhya Range) near Mhow, Madhya Pradesh
22590.why: Source text: near Mhow. End point is Bhareh, by the Pachnada confluence.

23685.name: Ganga River
23685.end: Via the Padma in Bangladesh; leaves India near Dhulian, West Bengal
23685.why: The dataset's Ganga line starts at Devprayag (the Bhagirathi is its own feature) and stops at the Bangladesh border, though Confluence says Bay of Bengal.

29220.name: Gomati River
29220.origin: Gomat Taal near Madho Tanda, Pilibhit district, Uttar Pradesh

29233.name: Bari Gandak Or Narayni
29233.origin: Mustang, Nepal, near the Tibet border, as the Kali Gandaki
29233.why: Upper part of the curated Gandak (29240). The 11 km of trace in Tibet is border noise.

29239.name: Yamuna River
29239.why: Source text: Yamunotri Glacier. Auto said '85 km NE of Dehradun'.

29240.name: Gandak River
29240.origin: Mustang, Nepal, near the Tibet border, as the Kali Gandaki
29240.why: Line starts about 30 km inside the border, too far for the automatic border-crossing check.

29252.name: Sone River
29252.why: Source text: Amarkantak highlands, Maikala range. Auto applied the Chota Nagpur label.

29296.name: Hooghly River
29296.why: The recorded end point (Kalyani) is not the mouth; Damodar joins this line near Diamond Harbour, so it runs to the sea.

29696.name: Sharda or Kali River
29696.why: Rises at Kalapani, which India administers; Natural Earth puts that start in Nepal. It is the India-Nepal border river, not one entering from Nepal.

30286.name: Rapti River
30286.entersAt: Near Bhinga, Shravasti district, Uttar Pradesh

30294.name: Ghaghara River
30294.why: Line begins at the Nepal border. The HydroRIVERS trace matched a side channel and stopped in Nepal, so the Tibetan source is declared by hand.

40025.name: Oshiwara
40025.why: Added from HydroRIVERS (data/added-rivers.json). Rises in the Aarey hills, not the Western Ghats, and drains into Malad Creek.
